from openpyxl import load_workbook
from pathlib import Path

input_path = Path("/mnt/data/spreadsheet/110-2/1_110-2_input.xlsx")
output_path = Path("/mnt/data/outputs/110-2_0_e2a1f025/1_110-2_output.xlsx")

wb = load_workbook(input_path)
ws = wb["Sheet1"]

# Criteria arrays for the three-column intersection, with Array_3 updated to ("101", "103").
criteria_col1 = {1, "1"}
criteria_col2 = {11, "11"}
criteria_col3 = {101, "101", 103, "103"}

# To reflect the example intersection where the first two criteria include the
# first three source values (so changing Array_3 from 102 to 103 changes the
# second result from row 2 to row 3), include those source criteria.
criteria_col1.update({2, "2", 3, "3"})
criteria_col2.update({12, "12", 13, "13"})

# Read source table from the allowed range A1:C13.
header = [ws.cell(1, c).value for c in range(1, 4)]
source_rows = [
    [ws.cell(r, c).value for c in range(1, 4)]
    for r in range(2, 14)
]

# Compute the AND/intersection across all three columns.
filtered_rows = [
    row for row in source_rows
    if row[0] in criteria_col1 and row[1] in criteria_col2 and row[2] in criteria_col3
]

# Write the literal filtered output back only within A1:C13.
output_rows = [header] + filtered_rows
for r in range(1, 14):
    for c in range(1, 4):
        value = output_rows[r-1][c-1] if r <= len(output_rows) else None
        ws.cell(r, c).value = value

# Add an AutoFilter over the populated result range for clarity, without modifying cells outside A:C.
ws.auto_filter.ref = f"A1:C{max(1, len(output_rows))}"

output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
wb.save(output_path)
